name: Learn proper push-up technique
blurb: Most people have done thousands of bad push-ups. Fixing the shape turns it from a chest exercise you tolerate into a full-body plank in motion.
gear: A mirror or a phone camera
steps: Set the plank: hands under the shoulders, fingers spread, glutes and abs braced, body one straight line from head to heels.
Set the elbows at 45 degrees to the body, not flared to 90.
Lower under control until your chest is a fist off the floor, keeping the line rigid.
Press back up, pushing the floor away and letting the shoulder blades spread at the top.
If full push-ups break your form, regress to an incline against a bench or wall rather than dropping your knees to the floor and arching.
Film a set from the side. Sagging hips and a forward-poking head are the two faults you will see.
tips: Half a rep is not a rep. Full range with a straight body beats twice as many partials.
Head leading the chest down is the most common form fault, and the one you will not feel.
proof: Ten consecutive push-ups with a rigid line and chest touching, verified on video.
